findings:
## Problem

The pipeline currently tracks effectively one ticker (AAPL) for governance signals, and the PR Newswire feed pulls global wire content with no ticker filtering. We need to expand coverage to a meaningful universe of US-listed companies without introducing:

1. **Rate limit violations** — EDGAR allows 10 req/s, we run at 2 RPS. Adding 500+ tickers naively means proportionally more concurrent polling.
2. **O(n²) or exponential complexity** — e.g. cross-joining every PR against every ticker on every pass, or re-scanning all historical filings when a new ticker is added.
3. **Memory/storage blowup** — unbounded ticker lists mean unbounded var/ directory growth.

## Required Design

### 1. Single curated watchlist file
Create `config/watchlist.json` — a single source of truth for all tickers the pipeline tracks. All processes (secwatch, prwatch, entity-graph, eps-processor, schd13-watcher) read from this file. No ticker is tracked unless it is in this file.

Structure:
```json
{
  "tickers": [
    { "symbol": "AAPL", "cik": "0000320193", "name": "Apple Inc." },
    { "symbol": "MSFT", "cik": "0000789019", "name": "Microsoft Corp." },
    ...
  ],
  "version": 1,
  "last_updated": "2026-05-31"
}
```

### 2. Suggested initial watchlist — S&P 100 subset (~50 tickers)
Start with 40-60 large-cap US names across sectors: AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, NVDA, TSLA, BRK.B, JPM, BAC, WFC, GS, MS, C, SCHW, JNJ, UNH, PFE, ABBV, LLY, XOM, CVX, COP, NEE, DUK, WMT, TGT, COST, HD, LOW, BA, CAT, GE, MMM, RTX, T, VZ, CMCSA, DIS, NFLX. This gives sector diversity without overwhelming the feed.

### 3. O(1) ticker lookup — use a map not a list scan
The ticker map must be loaded once at process startup into a `map[string]TickerInfo` keyed by symbol AND by CIK. PR body text matching must use exact symbol lookup against this map — not a linear scan of all tickers against all PR text. Complexity must be O(1) per PR, not O(n) per PR × n tickers.

### 4. PR Newswire ticker extraction — symbol matching only
For prwatch/prwatch-body, extract the ticker symbol from the PR metadata fields (pr newswire includes a `$TICKER` field in structured releases). Do NOT do fuzzy company name matching against the full watchlist — that is O(n) per document and will degrade as the list grows. If the metadata has no symbol, leave ticker as unknown rather than scanning.

### 5. EDGAR polling — one CIK at a time, sequential not parallel
secwatch must iterate the watchlist sequentially, one CIK per polling interval, not fan out all CIKs in parallel goroutines. Current 2 RPS budget divided across 50 tickers = one CIK checked every ~25 seconds. This is fine for near-real-time coverage of 8-K filings.

### 6. entity-graph — process only watchlisted tickers
entity-graph must skip any source document whose ticker is not in the watchlist map. This prevents unbounded growth of the entity graph if off-watchlist filings slip through.

### 7. Adding tickers must be O(1) operational cost
Adding a new ticker to `config/watchlist.json` should require zero code changes and zero reprocessing of historical data. The next poll cycle picks it up naturally.

## What NOT to do
- Do NOT dynamically discover tickers from PR text using NLP or fuzzy matching
- Do NOT fan out EDGAR requests in parallel per ticker
- Do NOT store a separate ticker config in each process — one file, all processes read it
- Do NOT backfill historical data when a ticker is added — forward-only from time of addition
suggested_fix:
1. Create config/watchlist.json with the ~50 ticker S&P 100 subset listed above, including CIK numbers for each.
2. Add a shared internal/watchlist/watchlist.go package that loads config/watchlist.json into map[string]TickerInfo (keyed by both symbol and CIK) at startup. All processes import this package — no process maintains its own ticker list.
3. In prwatch-body/eps-processor: replace any list-scan ticker matching with O(1) map lookup against the watchlist.
4. In secwatch: iterate watchlist.Tickers sequentially in the polling loop, one CIK per tick.
5. In entity-graph: add a watchlist guard at the top of the document processor — skip if ticker not in map.
6. Remove any hardcoded AAPL-only references throughout the codebase.
summary: Expand ticker coverage using a static curated watchlist — not dynamic discovery — to avoid O(n²) and rate limit issues
